Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: corrective FRONT production drawing of the approved M09 patrol labor robot.
Input 1 is the EXACT ADOPTED MASTER and sole design authority: use its large full-body robot at left for BODY PROPORTIONS, its large head closeup at top center for EXACT HEAD IDENTITY, and small rear view for wall inventory. The previous front derivative was rejected for squat bulk and wrong head. Reconstruct the true FRONT of THIS MASTER without redesigning or cartooning it.
ONE full-body direct front view, portrait 1024x1536 on white, complete head/fins and feet in frame, enough margins. Adult service robot, visibly upright, athletic and substantial with long usable thighs/shins and a distinct waist. Preserve master's balanced limb thickness; do not make it skinny or extremely tall. The master has a defined narrowing lower torso, space between rib armor and pelvis, shoulders with a gentle dome, not inflated round ball shoulders. Keep chest approximately the mother's width relative to the head and hips; avoid massive broad barrel chest and short abdominal segment. Do not enlarge head or shorten pelvis-to-floor length. Slightly relaxed stance, legs moderately apart, both arms down, left elbow naturally a little bent to hold wall.
HEAD IS CRITICAL: accurately rotate the master's closeup head into front view. Keep its relatively narrow upright patrol helmet with small amber roof lamp, slate upper forehead plate, ivory brim around a dark inset visor with two small cyan eyes. Keep the master's SINGLE angular ivory lower-face shield/mouth mask and narrow tapered chin. No invented second stacked chin/white beard, no wide toothy/grinning jaw, no wide puck helmet or crushed forehead. Ear service housings and modest rectangular rear/up fins must be copied from master at matching proportions/direction, not inflated tall rabbit ears or new pointed horns. The mask silhouette is the same as master, only frontal projection changes.
COLOR AND SURFACES: same warm ivory broad continuous curved shells, slate grey-blue chest band/shoulder cap/knee cap/toe, fine red reflective stripes, black rubber joint gaiters; clean expressive black outlines, warm cel shading, light maintenance scratches like master, no new logos.
EQUIPMENT: one unfolded flat ivory/slate traffic wall with red diagonal band held in ANATOMICAL LEFT hand (viewer RIGHT), beside body from near shoulder to near ankle. Backpack contains FIVE narrow folded wall modules ONLY: three on robot RIGHT (front viewer LEFT), two on robot LEFT (front viewer RIGHT). From front only top rails and partial side edges naturally visible, not a huge wide extra armored chest. FIVE carried + ONE held = SIX, no extra wall. Right hand relaxed open. No other subjects/insets/text. This must look like the SAME accepted service machine from input1, with its original correct head and adult proportion, not a new helmet or military infantry armor.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: vehicle-mode production drawing sheet for M10 fire/bridge transforming service robot.
Input1 is APPROVED M10 source master: upper-right TRUCK is the exact vehicle silhouette and chassis organization; lower-right is deployed bridge work mode. Input2 is current humanoid FRONT fixing part identities, two windshield panes, exactly six wheels, right waist twin tanks and left hose reel. Preserve approved orange/ivory engineering design. Make a professional colored technical illustration sheet of the SAME three-axle truck in TRANSPORT/STOWED mode only.
Composition: wide landscape 1800x1200 white/light ivory sheet. Large TRUE SIDE view across upper half, cab pointing LEFT. Lower half contains matched true FRONT at left and true REAR at right, both level straight orthographic-like views. Clearly separated with fine grey baselines, ample margins, no background scenery. Only these THREE vehicle views, no humanoid, no quadruped, no alternate truck redesign. Tiny neat headings EXACTLY "SIDE", "FRONT", "REAR".
Vehicle identity: low flat-front rescue truck cab, ivory pillars, EXACTLY TWO broad dark teal front windscreen panes and two wipers, amber roof beacons, rectangular amber headlights and orange bumper/lower grille. Broad engineering wheels with orange hubs, exactly THREE road axles / SIX wheels total: one front axle below cab and tandem rear axles; no fourth axle/spares. Ivory/orange service-box chassis behind cab with same red latches, dark teal details and graphite mechanical frame.
The robot's TWO long flat bridge-leaf back packs are stowed HORIZONTALLY lengthwise on roof/chassis, side by side in width, not extra copies, no giant wing panels. Each pack has paired/hinged/telescoping deck sections with ivory upper plate, orange end caps, dark teal long recesses and silver/black understructure, matching source master's same two packs. In rear projection show TWO end faces side by side plus a central narrow gap and bridge hinges, NOT one arbitrary slab, and maintain same total width as chassis.
TWO ivory tanks with teal inspection bands/red caps reside together behind cab on VEHICLE RIGHT SIDE (physical assignment same as robot right waist); pump/hose reel on vehicle LEFT. On chosen RIGHT-SIDE view both tanks can be visible, opposite pump occluded; front/rear respect actual sides (front viewer left=vehicle right, rear viewer right=vehicle right). FOUR stabilizer outriggers, two each side, folded close in side-locker housings while travelling. No deployed feet on this transport sheet. Normal vehicle clearance, no robot face on cab, no arms sticking out. Provide traceable joints/panel seams and plausible part boundaries without excessive tiny labels. Same black ink outlines, cel-shaded color, fine service wear and confident detail level as source. No logos or borrowed franchise marks.
